anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet, the two logic-input pins of the high-side switch U6 (TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) – IN (pin 1) and DIAG_EN (pin 2) – are joined together and run right to the +12V node that also carries the C1 0.1uF capacitor (the node fed by the +12V power symbol), i.e. they sit on the +12V rail together with U6's VS pin 8. No HEATER label appears anywhere at U6; the HEATER label appears only at U1 pin 13 (ESP32 GPIO1), at the J5 screw terminal and at D2/R3.
anomalies.expected: U6's IN and DIAG_EN inputs should be driven by the ESP32 GPIO1 HEATER control net so the firmware can switch the heater (spec: "IN/DIAG_EN (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 (net /Microcontroller/HEATER)"), with only VS (pin 8) tied to +12V.

evidence.quote: `IN`/`DIAG_EN` (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 (net `/Microcontroller/HEATER`)
Microcontroller sheet: U6 pins '2 DIAG_EN' and '1 IN' join and continue right to the '+12V' power symbol / 'C1 0.1uF' node; the 'HEATER' label is present only at U1 pin 13 and at J5/D2.

anomalies.impact: The smart high-side switch is permanently enabled whenever 12 V is present at the barrel jack: the heater cannot be turned off by the firmware (bang-bang control is lost), the oven can overheat, and the D2 'heater on' indicator is driven by a GPIO1 net that no longer reaches the switch, so indication no longer matches the actual heater state.

parsed.summary: The Microcontroller sheet shows U6's IN/DIAG_EN logic inputs tied to the +12V rail node (with C1) instead of to the ESP32 GPIO1 HEATER net, so the heater switch would be permanently on and uncontrollable; all other reviewed sections (power mux, buck regulator, thermocouple SPI bus and chip selects, fan interfaces, USB-C CC resistors) match the specification.
